questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Pre-Modern World' refers to.
questions.a: Before the modern era of nations and formal trade agreements, people across the world were connected through travel, migration, trade and the exchange of ideas, crops, diseases and technologies over long distances.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Pre-Modern World'.
questions.a: Global interconnectedness is not a modern phenomenon; long-distance cultural and economic exchanges shaped the pre-modern world.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Pre-Modern World' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Introduction to Globalisation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Silk Routes Link the World' refers to.
questions.a: Silk routes were a network of overland and maritime trade paths that connected East Asia to the Mediterranean and Europe, carrying silk, goods, culture and religion across vast distances for centuries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Silk Routes Link the World'.
questions.a: The silk routes were early arteries of global trade and cultural exchange, linking regions through commerce and religion.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Silk Routes Link the World' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Pre-Modern World

concepts.title: Food Travels: Spread of New Crops

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Food Travels: Spread of New Crops' refers to.
questions.a: The discovery and conquest of the Americas introduced new crops such as potatoes, maize, tomatoes, chillies and sweet potatoes to Europe and Asia, dramatically changing global diets and populations.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Food Travels: Spread of New Crops'.
questions.a: The movement of new crops from the Americas transformed food habits and supported population growth in Europe and Asia.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Food Travels: Spread of New Crops' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Pre-Modern World

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Conquest, Disease and Trade' refers to.
questions.a: European conquest of the Americas was aided by the spread of germs like smallpox, which decimated indigenous populations, while precious metals from the Americas fuelled European trade with Asia.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Conquest, Disease and Trade'.
questions.a: Disease, conquest and trade were intertwined; germs enabled conquest and silver from the Americas integrated global trade.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Conquest, Disease and Trade' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Pre-Modern World

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'A World Economy Takes Shape' refers to.
questions.a: By the nineteenth century, a global economy emerged through trade in goods, labour and capital, supported by colonies, new technologies and the migration of millions of people.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'A World Economy Takes Shape'.
questions.a: A true world economy took shape in the nineteenth century through trade, migration and capital flows across regions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'A World Economy Takes Shape' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Nineteenth Century (1815-1914)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Role of Technology' refers to.
questions.a: Technological advances such as railways, steamships, the telegraph and the Suez Canal transformed transportation and communication, making global trade faster and cheaper.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Role of Technology'.
questions.a: Technology shrank the world by reducing the time and cost of trade and communication, enabling closer global integration.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Role of Technology' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Nineteenth Century (1815-1914)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Late Nineteenth-Century Colonialism' refers to.
questions.a: In the late nineteenth century, European powers expanded colonial control over Africa and Asia, restructuring local economies to supply raw materials and food for the growing world economy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Late Nineteenth-Century Colonialism'.
questions.a: Colonial expansion reorganised economies in Africa and Asia to serve the needs of the industrial world economy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Late Nineteenth-Century Colonialism' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Nineteenth Century (1815-1914)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Inter-War Economy' refers to.
questions.a: The First World War caused massive destruction and debt; the post-war period saw economic instability, the Great Depression of 1929, and the collapse of the first phase of globalisation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Inter-War Economy'.
questions.a: War, debt and the Great Depression disrupted the interconnected world economy built in the nineteenth century.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Inter-War Economy' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Inter-War Economy

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Bretton Woods Institutions' refers to.
questions.a: The 1944 Bretton Woods Conference established the IMF and the World Bank to stabilise currencies and finance post-war reconstruction, creating a framework for the post-war global economy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Bretton Woods Institutions'.
questions.a: The Bretton Woods system created institutions to manage currency stability and development finance, shaping the post-war economy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Bretton Woods Institutions' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Rebuilding a World Economy: The Post-War Era

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Decolonisation and Globalisation' refers to.
questions.a: After 1945, decolonisation created new nations in Asia and Africa, while from the 1970s onwards the Bretton Woods system weakened and a new phase of globalisation emerged through trade, finance and multinational corporations.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Decolonisation and Globalisation'.
questions.a: Decolonisation and the later shift to flexible exchange rates and global finance marked a new phase of globalisation.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Decolonisation and Globalisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Rebuilding a World Economy: The Post-War Era
